result: Workspace-source live Process-worker test passed: 1 passed in 20.24s.
assertions: The accepted submission stores a credential alias, not the original or rotated PostgreSQL password, in its canonical execution snapshot.

After the dispatch was durable and before the Process worker claimed the submission, the test rotated the environment-backed sink credential to a dedicated PostgreSQL role with access only to the test sink and effect-ledger tables.
The worker resolved the current credential at execution time, recovered from a hard kill during the preceding source-artifact write, and completed the sink write using the rotated role.
The recovered run retained one committed effect and the expected PostgreSQL row; the temporary test role and its grants were removed after the run.

limitations: This verifies one environment-backed credential rotation between dispatch and claim. It does not cover a production identity provider, credential expiration, rotation at every acceptance/dispatch/claim boundary, or tenant-adversarial credential revocation.
This is local workspace-source evidence for CPython 3.11.15, Prefect 3.7.8, PostgreSQL 16.13, and the Process pool; remote CI and the complete supported-version and hosting matrix remain open.
